summary.text: 杯 means “cup” or “drinking vessel.” A common analysis treats 木 as semantic and 不 as a proposed sound component. A received account of the related graph 桮 instead assigns the sound role to 否; the relationship between these accounts and the earliest form is unresolved.

formation.text: The common proposed construction is phonosemantic: 木 contributes a vessel-related category, and 不 is a sound cue. The received account of 桮 instead identifies 否 as its sound element. How these analyses relate to the earliest form remains unresolved.

components.text: 木 appears on the left of 杯 and contributes the vessel-related semantic category in the 木 + 不 analysis. No distinct earlier form for 木 in 杯 is established.

不 appears on the right of 杯. One analysis assigns it a phonetic role. In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction, 杯 *plɯː and 不 *pɯ, *pɯʔ, or *pɯ' share an initial and rhyme nucleus but differ in the reconstructed lateral and vowel length. Its role in the earliest graph remains unsettled.

sound.text: Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstructions compare 杯 *plɯː with 不 *pɯ, *pɯʔ, or *pɯ'. Their shared initial and rhyme nucleus support a proposed sound-series relationship despite differences in the reconstructed lateral and vowel length.

components.text: 否 belongs to the received account of 桮, a graph historically related to 杯: that account identifies 否 as 桮’s phonetic element. It does not establish that 否 changed into 不 or that 否 is a component of modern 杯.

sound_limitation.text: The account identifies 否 as the phonetic element in 桮 but supplies no pronunciation comparison for 否 and 桮 in a named system.

history.text: The received Shuowen account concerns 桮 rather than 杯: it describes 桮 as 木 with phonetic 否 and does not include 杯. Duan Yucai is reported to call 杯 a vulgar form, which later became standard. This connects the graphs without establishing their precise sequence or how their components relate.

Other analyses read modern 杯 as 木 + 不. One scholarly proposal connects 不 with a hollowed tree remnant, but no early inscription confirms this interpretation. The evidence does not settle whether 不 was original or later read into the graph, and does not establish graphic corruption.
The forms 𠤯, 柸, 桮, 㮎, and 盃 are listed as variants of 杯, but their chronology and graphic paths are unresolved. Today, 盃 is often used for an award or trophy.

uncertainties.text: The earliest written form and chronology of the variants remain unresolved. The evidence also does not settle whether 不 was an original sound component or a later analysis of the graph.
The comparison with Tibetan phor pa does not establish a borrowing direction or the historical name for a cup. A sound-based borrowing account for 杯 is not demonstrated.

senses.period: attested in the received Mencius passage; manuscript date unresolved
senses.text: In the received Mencius passage, 一杯水 means “a cup of water,” an early textual use of 杯 for a vessel. The citation does not date the surviving physical witness or establish the word’s earliest occurrence.
杯 is also used as a classifier for cupfuls. Examples from Mencius and later works are listed, but they do not establish when this use developed in relation to the vessel sense.

senses.gloss: award or trophy, especially in the form 盃
senses.text: The variant 盃 is often used for an award or trophy. When this use arose is unresolved.

limitations.text: The Mencius citation supports the vessel sense but does not date the surviving manuscript or establish the earliest physical witness. The evidence does not show when classifier or trophy uses arose relative to the vessel sense.

overview.text: 杯 means “cup” or “drinking vessel.” In a common analysis, 木 marks the vessel category and 不 is a proposed sound cue. An older account assigns the sound role to 否 in the related form 桮.

components.text: In this analysis, 木 points to the vessel category.
不 is a proposed sound element, though its role in the earliest form is unsettled.
否 belongs to the older account of 桮, a graph related to 杯; it is not an established part of modern 杯.

relationships.text: In the 木 + 不 analysis of 杯, 木 contributes the vessel category.
One analysis treats 不 as the sound component. Zhengzhang’s reconstructions support a proposed sound-series relationship but do not establish the earliest graph.
The received Shuowen account concerns 桮, while 杯 later became standard; their exact graphic sequence is unresolved.
The received account identifies 否 as the phonetic element in 桮, without establishing it as a component of modern 杯.
